statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 entries
Each entry s_i is either plus 1 or minus 1
a is a permutation of the set {1, 2, ..., n}
The inequality must hold for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
The expression a_{i+1} minus a_i is compared through strict inequality, so equality is not allowed
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, characterize all length n minus 1 sequences of signs plus 1 or minus 1 that maximize the number of permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} whose successive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: For each integer n at least 2
For each sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1
Define f(s) as the number of permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} such that for every i from 1 to n minus 1, s_i times (a_{i+1} minus a_i) is greater than 0
Among all such sequences s for the fixed n, find those that maximize f(s)
